edits.title: Vedapuriswara Koyil Brahmotsavam Ends with Utsava Shanti and Shankhabhishekam

children.text: Brahmotsavam Day 16, Shankhabhishekam. Went for this at 10:30am. Homam going on, Arjun gurukkal (who was the main priest during the whole Brahmotsavam) leading. Abhishekam was happening, we caught the tail end of it. Homa finished, the 2 kalasa were taken by Arjun and Kalyana Sundara Gurukkals one round about the prakaram, coconut phat near the dhvajastambha, and then the main kalasa into the moola sthanam – Presumably 108 shankha for abhishekam, done one by one unlike Chetty Koyil where it was being done a few at a time – then shift over to Amman sannathi for the second kalasa pour – simple alankaram and deeparadhanai.
The day's schedule:
9:00 AM - Utsava Shanti, Shankhabhishekam (Conch Abhishekam).

edits.title: Vidaiyatri: Of swings and pearl carriages

children.text: The kalasa thirumanjanam happened in the morning for the moolavar. Later there was a dwadasa aradhanam, with the showing of twelve lamps.

The Sapthavarna Puranam recitation was by Ramanan Bhattacharya after the return of the procession. The Sapthavarna Puranam/Sathavaranam Puranam is a traditional devotional text dedicated to Lord Surya, focusing on his 21 names and attributes that remove sins, overcome illness, and bring prosperity.

Saptavaranam, Saptāvaraṇam: Seven square enclosures, one within the other, the innermost containing the central shrine, as at Śrīraṅgam; கோயிலைச் சுற்றி அமைந்த ஏழு பிராகாரங்கள்/ koyilais surri amaintha ezhu piragarangal.
Brahmotsavam Day 10, Vidaiyatri Day 1 Schedule:
10:00 AM: 108 Kalasa Thirumanjanam
04:30 PM: Dwadasa Aradhanam
07:00 PM: Chandra Prabhai Procession and Sapthavarna Puranam recitation

edits.title: A day of Brahmanda Brahmotsavam Events
Vedapuriswara Koyil gets ready for its Brahmotsavam

children.text: We happened to be at the Vedapuriswara Koyil this morning, and noticed the ongoing preparations of an all-utsavars-abhishekam. The patrikai did not include this, but we were lucky to be present at the time – or rather exceedingly before time since the delayed ubhayakaras kept everyone waiting, as happens at so many temples all the time. The abhishekam itself though, once it begins, is greatly exciting. The presence of the Somaskandamurti is majestic and vast – one that cannot go un-acknowledged.
At 530pm the Adigu Vinayakar abhishekam was already underway and nearly complete. Arun was unable to come.

The Vinayaka utsavar was brought outside the Vinayaka shrine and dressed up for the evening purappadu. All the other vahanas in dazzling silver were on the other prakaram. A Thiruvasagam group sitting before the Nayanar sannathi continued singing as the Vinayakar puja carried on. It’s Thursday, so Dakshinamurti is also being propitiated nearby. Ayyappan Swami calls me over and gives a mango and a flower from the Murugan sannathi during the sayaraksha naivedyam rounds.

After Vinayaka’s deeparadhanai, the vastu puja begins right in front of the dhvajastambha, conducted by Venkatesa gurukkal who had done the Chetty Brahmotsavam.  He calls two younger sivacharyas over to chant the Brahma suktam, Rudra suktam, and the Vastu gayatri - "Om Vaastunaathaaya Vidmahe, Chaturbhujaaya Dheemah, Tanno Vaastuh Prachodayaat". By the northern entrance, on the floor, is a form of the goddess made in putthu mannu – “anthill-sand”. This is for the Mrtsangrahanam puja. The vastu puja concludes with the burning of the straw vastu effigy, and its dragging for one round around the temple accompanied by thavil on a single, haunting, ominous beat. The man who drags the effigy around is presented with a dhoti before doing so (Arasoo mama calls me over to take a photo), and is only to step back into the temple after bathing.

Vinayaka meanwhile is ready and arrives at the Mrtsangrahanam site, where a puja happens not unlike the one for Thulasi Mariamman at the smeared stone on the footpath. Numerous shanti mantras are heard, a grid is made with kusha grass with rice in each cadre, and milk is poured and flowers are offered on the manvetti. The manvetti is then used to take some of the earth that forms the goddess figure who is dressed in red. Milk is then poured on the “eaten” body, and the collected earth goes into a Kalavai Satti like thing. It is covered with the same red cloth, now bunched and tied so the tied part sits upright like a figure. A malli garland is wrapped around this red upright cloth knot, and the entire basked of earth is placed at Vinayaka’s feet. The purappadu continues until it reaches the utsavar sannathi in South-West corner.

One of the families whose ubhayam this is runs the Sundara Vinayaka temple (built/ begun in 1910). Rani ma’m, together with her husband and a niece from Chennai are the ones sponsoring this event. Once again, it is this network of temple links that leads us on, and Sundara Vinayaka becomes a temple in our list to document.

Mannivannan comes over, introduces me and Arun to the EO, who seems quite friendly and supportive. We also meet other of his friends who seem social media buffs, and Meenakshi who does accounts in the office. She is to introduce me to Gurumama later. Guru mama I also meet but briefly just before the ubhayakara puja in the main shrine, so he’s a little short. Nothing else noteworthy.
Evening preparatory pujas included: Anugnai, Vigneswara Puja and Vastu Shanti

edits.title: Chetty Koyil Visit, Of Kaalams and Gradations
Slowly, slowly at the Perumal Koyil
Getting to know the Srinivasa Perumal Koyil–or not
Chetty Koyil Rahu Kala Durga Puja
Kamakshi Amman Koyil with Gurukkal and Periyavar

children.text: Sunday evening. Arun finds the Kannika Parameswari is out on a veethi ula! So we run about and get a few photos – the procession route is long, winding N-S down the main roads and she returns to the temple only around midnight. Kannika Parameswari Jayanti (Vasavi Jayanti) is celebrated annually on the tenth day (Dasami) of the bright fortnight in the Telugu month of Vaisakha. The Iyer seems very happy, garlanding and blessing all those who come to pay respects!

We sit for an hour or more with the very busy Sriram Gurukkal to understand the annual ritual practices at Angalamman in Angalanagar. He is often interrupted by calls and people coming in with work and requests, but is very patient with us and everyone who comes to him. We often see him in the temple talking to young neighborhood boys who throng about the place. It is just him and the older Gurukkal managing the Angalamman temple. It appears that they function as much as guides and mentors as priests.

edits.title: Two Ramanujar processions in a day

children.text: We also make a quick visit to the Lawspet Siva Subramania Swami temple, where Ramanan Gurukkal helps out the main priest (Venkatesan Gurukkal). There is a group of women singing there, led by one Kalyani mami. This temple has an easy laid back atmosphere. Steady stream of devotees, but no special pujas going on at the time we go.
Krittikai puja is usually a morning abhishekam to utsavar-Valli-Devasena, and Moolavar and a simple alankaram in the evening followed by deeparadhanai, and a thanga-ther ul-purappadu.

edits.title: The Keeper of Perumal's Ritual Calendar

children.text: Revathi’s father Sekar mama sits with us a long while to explain the temple’s utsavam schedule. He is the man behind the Kodanda Rama Bhaktar group, and in many ways the keeper of Perumal's calendar. He introduces us to the temple’s Maṇiyakkarar, who attends to both this and the Sivan Koyil since the two temples are managed by a joint administration with a government-appointed EO (Executive Officer) at the helm. He is very helpful and advises us (in effect) to come in as bhaktas. Everyone takes photos, so what’s to stop us from doing the same, in that capacity. We are also introduced to Rajagopala Thathacharya, who is a goldmine of stories, songs, and insights. He is the one who first tells us that this temple draws its lineage from the Thiruvahindrapuram Perumal temple, which is one of the 108 Divya Desams–this temple is its “abhimana sthalam.”

Atthi Varada figure in the Nirvagam office. Made for the prior kumabhishekam, should have been “released” into a water body, in Saiva temples it’s burned to ash, but here it’s an “adbhutamana” figure and so they’ve kept it with nool malai.

edits.title: The Keepers of the Chetty Koyil and Krittikai

children.text: We go to meet the Gurukkal and Nirvagam head at the Chetty Koyil this evening. Much to learn about how ritual calendars are organized and under what circumstances temples continue to function. We take it for granted that the temple gets rental income from its surrounding properties, but these can be uncertain and precarious sources.

The Nirvagam head (Shankarnarayana Chettiar) tells us about the Ayira Vysya community whose temple this is. The community’s origin story is one not unlike that of the Arya Vysyas (whose temple Kannika Parameswari is), and will be recorded in our other notes. The similarity of names is striking, but perhaps a coincidence. Both are prominent merchant groups in Pondicherry. The community and its shrine have been around from colonial times, as we know well from entries in Ananda Rangapillai’s diaries (1736 to 1761), and have played no small role in protecting and ensuring the continuity of Hindu practices in the town. Murtis from the destroyed Vedapuriswara temple were brought here for safekeeping, we have often been told.

A unique feature of the Chetty Koyil, as it is commonly known, is that it houses both Siva and Visnu temples in the same complex. Why? Because Chettiars themselves are both Saiva and Vaishnava. (We find something similar at Kannika Parameswari, which pays obeisance to both Rama, Andal etc. as well as deities in the lineage of Siva).

After all our conversations, there is a Murugan abhishekam and ul-purappadu to mark Krittikai, around 730pm - 830pm. Shankaranarayana Chettiar is there unfailingly for every event. It's hard to imagine this temple without his presence, and we've only been around a short time.

Spent a lovely 45 minutes at Mutthumariamman. Met with a young pusari Narayanaswamy who is but a boy studying Tamil at the Pondicherry University, and with Prakash who works at the temple, following after his mother who also used to work here. They tell us enthusiastically about the special alankaram done on Aadi Fridays, when the goddess is adorned with velli ornaments. He showed us pictures of the goddess adorned with fruits all around (Thai masam). And also Chithirai Pournami, when she is adorned with all white.

When asked about the Ellai Amman connection, he tells us that there wasn’t any collective veethi ula with all the three ammans together. Instead, three times a year, when Mutthumariamman goes for a veethi ula, she goes upto the ellai (border) of Ellaiamman – this happens till date. They mention the Ezhai Mariamman, Mutthumariamman and Ellai Amman as being a sort of trio. The three veethi ulas are: Masi Maham, Brahmotsavam (Thai Masam), Aandu Vizha (Aavani Masam).

For Masi Maham the amman from Melmalayanur (Angalamman) comes down to Pondicherry. On her way, she stops at a Bala Tripura Sundari temple (the one near Irumbai?). She arrives in Pondy one day prior to Masi Maham, and spends that night at Mutthumariamman temple here. After masi maham theerthavari, she returns to Mutthumariamman, and then she has an Unjal Utsavam the same day or the next, when she leaves for the Vedapuriswara temple. There she has an entire veethi ula with Siva. After this, she heads back to Melmalayanur. On the way back home, drops by Bala Tripura Sundari again and then heads home. These journeys seem as much planned for historical reasons as for practical ones for those accompanying deities on these long travels.

The Mutthumariamman temple has Katavarayan as a protective deity, apart from also having Pavadarayan and his wife (which is unusual, he’s usually not shown as a married man). There is Pecchayiamman, who has an unusually shanta roopam instead of the regular ugra.
There is also an Anjaneyar shrine, unusual for an Amman shrine. But it’s an old one, to which Prathishtha had been done from long before, so it was never removed during the temple’s expansion.

The pusari and Prakash also tell us that this is a kula deivam for many local Tamils who now live in France – there is some evidence for this on the stone inscriptions at the back of the temple. He says also that the Ellaiamman koyil may well be built fast because there’s support for it from those who take it as their kula deivam.
So of course we ask the priests at the Kamakshi Amman temple about the Ellaiamman connection, and the story becomes a lot more complex fast.

Vedapuriswara, accompanied by Kamakshi amman, would go to Ellaiamman’s temple, all sisters after all, and the three deities would then remain at different places in the town – at the end of the Kamakshi amman road (the priest pointed east), near the lighthouse (as far down as the lighthouse/marina), and then what sounded to me like the end of anna Salai near the botanical garden, so that people from each of these locations could come. The trio would stop for a few hours in each place. This festival was once a 3 day affair. It has since shrunk and dried up considerably, owing in part to the destruction of the Vedapuriswara Koyil and to the ban in Dupleix’s time (the priest says) to processions and temple ceremonies.

One room next to the one with Utsava murtis is dedicated to the Balalaya Chithiram or Balalaya Oviyam (etched wooden images of planned temple forms) for the upcoming Kumbhabhishekam. As long as the construction plan is in progress, there will be no Brahmostavam.
The Puducherry Kamakshi Amman is shown standing, and is seen to have a different appearance from the Kanchipuram and Mangadu Kamakshi Ammans
(cf. Murugesan’s article on this temple, v1 408)
Went in the morning, around 1030. Saw preparations for the evening. Stands and trays have been arranged for Deepams to be lit and placed.

44th Anjaneyar Abhishekam for Varsha Pirappu just began. Watched about half of it and left. Remarked that abhishekam items were being used very generously. Apparently this anjaneyar abhishekam tradition began 44 years ago to mimic the same tradition already existing at Thiruvahindrapuram in Cuddalore. A bhaktar used to go there regularly, saw the ceremonial marking and sought to reproduce it here.

We went again at 730pm, the Ramanujar utsavam chanting was about to begin (Deepa got chastised for not having a pottu! It had fallen off. Used kunkumam and looked like mahakali for the rest of the evening). 4 priests sat in front of the Ramanujar shrine and chanted from the Prabandham, closing as always with Periyalvar’s “Pallandu pallandu,” which never fails to move: பல்லாண்டு பல்லாண்டு பல்லாயிரத்தாண்டு பலகோடி நூறாயிரம்

மல்லாண்ட திண்தோள் மணிவண்ணா! உன் சேவடி செவ்வித் திருக்காப். It is not mere closing but a maṅgalāśāsanam, as we will learn—uttering protective blessings for the Lord, expressing the devotee's anxious concern that nothing should befall the Lord's sacred form.

We watched people light lamps and mill around the Anjaneyar shrine which was still active (and he looked super smart in embroidered clothes, set amidst so many colorful flowers), spoke to the lady removing leaves from Tulasi bunches who has been here doing this work for 20 years, she says – people offer tulasi, it gets tied/comes tied in bunches, goes to the sannathis and comes out for her to remove leaves – then is distributed again from the perumal sannathi.
"Perumakoil" is the local colloquialism for Perumal Koil. Say it fast, you'll see.

edits.title: Kodanda Rama's Utsavam ends with Panakam

children.text: As we enter the temple, there is a private bhajanai group singing before the Pandarinathar shrine. Apparently they gather here every Sunday from 6 to 7, and it’s open for anyone to join. They come from different parts of town, and on Saturdays, they have longer bhajanai sessions at the Pandarinathar shrines close to their respective homes.

Thiruvonam nakshatram today, Perumal’s nakshatram–marks the formal close to the Ramar Utsavam. We go at 7pm. Puja is a simple one, no special alankaram for Rama, simple (gorgeous!) veshti, a few malli malais and a strand of malli tied around his crown – it was the most beautiful. We are told to come back day after tomorrow, April 14 for “Laksha deepam” in the evening – it’s Tamil New year that day.

After the puja we sit (Aruna Mami from Chetty koyil is here and keeps a space for me) and everyone gets a leaf. Panakam comes directly in bare hands only, just enough to catch and slurp in reverence. The rest is a simple Kosambari and a thair saadam which is more rice than curd but delicious.
Monday, April 13 begins 10 days of the Ramanuja utsavam. Not a moment to spare!

Ramar Utsavam penultimate day, Day 24. Arun goes for this. Nadaswaram team already performing as I enter at 730pm. As one enters, to the left of the Dhvavajastambha on the prakara, an entire stage has been set up for them. The bell is also being sounded by the same dedicated gentleman Deepa di and I met the other day. Utsava murtis are in their chamber, behind the drawn curtain.
The unjal utsavam is to happen in the Vasanta Mandapam on the temple’s north east corner, and it is kept lit.

There’s a long queue for the Varadaraja shrine, but as I join and complete my darshan, it seems to be just a regular line, perhaps crowded simply because of the utsavam that is about to begin. I also notice the golden lizards in the ardhamandapa. The circumambulatory path around the garbhagrha is closed on the right. So one can walk past the garbhagrha to the left, but must exit from the opening at the back which faces the Narasimha shrine.

Rama comes out soon, and the procession is very festive. The music is slow and sublime, matched by Rama’s gracious swaying advance. He goes around the temple, pausing multiple times for significant durations, lost in the alai of the music. Upon reaching the ardhamandapa he takes some time behind curtains again as he is raised onto the dais and made comfortable upon the unjal. And once his beloved Anjaneyar is brought to him, the curtains open and we discover Rama in all his reposed glory. A few moments of magic when the electricity goes off periodically, leaving the entire scene lit dimly by the few deepams – there can be no sight more intimately immersive.
Right across Rama, facing him from their dedicated stage, are the Nadaswaram team with their singer, presenting music up to 1am. By the time the priests go home it’s 230am!

1030am when we get there, and there is a Thirumanjanam going on in the Kodandarama shrine. Done simultaneously to both the utava murtis and the main murtis in the shrine. It’s very beautiful, several have gathered–men inside the enclosure, others sitting on either side outside. The process is the same as we’ve seen elsewhere, except that every time a substance is washed off, there is dhoopam (with dhoopakal), deepam (with kodi vilakku) - thattu vilakku, ie thrice.

One of the security guards helps us understand where photography is permitted (though the contradiction of important people taking photos of the moolasthanams and the practice otherwise being forbidden is evident). People are aware of the many contradictions that structure the daily functioning of the temple, but they find ways to make peace–by speaking of the importance of true devotion, God’s attention to us all regardless of status etc. Or at least they say they do!

edits.title: What a way to enter the Perumal Koyil!

children.text: Shankhabhishekam from 9 to noon. Very very beautiful the abhishekam of all the utsava murtis. Completion concludes the Brahmotsavam. Got to sit and have a small chat with Venkatesa Gurukkal, while the abhishekam was still being prepared. The Shankhabhishekam done on the main inner lingam was such a strong experience. Induced a very intimate self-giving.
Here is the rough schedule:
919am, Chanting at yaga salai, while Shankhas are made ready inside.
Preparations on vandi, all utsavamurtis loaded and taken to mandapa area. Arranged on elevated benches. Order (left to right):
Ganesha, Murugan + consorts, Somaskanda (with Parvati and baby Skanda), the Astramurti, Chandrasekara with Gauri, Gnanambika + Candikeshvara
935am, Deeparadhanai at Karpaka Vinaayaka shrine at back, to start things off
940am, Nadaswaram team playing, seemingly by themselves.
945am, With venkatesa gurukkal, chatting about how the Shankhabhishekam marks the end of Brahmotsavam and how shankhas bring punyam.
1000am, Mulamurti and Gnanambigai Ambhishekam
1024am, Utsavamurti abhishekam
1051am, Rosewater waiting in kalasa. All paused. Maybe waiting for shankhas?
Plenty of smoke coming from yaga salai
1112am, Yaga salai gathering, chanting, music. Deeparadhanai – preparations for the Kalasa purappadu. Pori poured into a flat basket, held by thalaivar. Pori handed out to devotees.

1120am, Kalasa purappadu. 2 Kalasas from yaga salai loaded onto two priests heads. Pori throwing on them before dhvajastambha. Walking around pradakshina. Music is fabulous. High tempo as pradakshina completes.
1130am, Shankhas brought. Shankhas water filled. Two large shankhas. Rest small.
Meanwhile priests with kalasa go into garbhagrha. For kalasabhishekam.
Now shankhas also taken into garbhagrha. Shankhabhishekam follows. Shankha water being poured on Linga one by one.
Looked like there were two rounds. First 108 shankha water was poured. Next the 108 shankhas were emptied of their flowers and leaves put within.
1147am, Over. Deeparadhanai. Flames brought out. Whole troop moves to gnanambigai shrine. Kalasa water poured. Big shankha water poured. Deeparadhanai.
Kalasa brought out with aradhanai flame. Everybody moving out to utsavamurtis.
Kalasas both brought to utsava murti.
Rusrakha mala on kalatisvara, ornaments on others for swarnabhishekam. Kalasa water abhishekam on all. Deeparadhanai.
1154am, Abhishekam ornaments taken off of utsavamurtis and returned to those who offered them. Kalasa water sprinkled on devotees. Then the Utsavamurtis taken for alankaram behind screen.
1200 noon. I think I'm done. It'll take another hour for alankaram. The waiting! Then a final puja and prasadam will be served.

edits.title: Lawspet, the morning after Panguni Utthiram
A Lone Theerthavari on Panguni Utthiram

children.text: Shankhabhishekam. No photos in this temple, so all we can do is take notes for whatever little we're able to ask the priests. They've a steady stream of work after all. How do they get to the sahasra-shankhas, I wonder. Perhaps by repeating the same process across puja kaalams?
7am second kalam yaga pujai, Visesha homam Divahuti, Mahapurnahuti, Deeparadhanai,
1030am Yattiradanam, Kalasa purappadu, Moolavar Kalasabhishekam, 1008 Shankhabhishekam and 108 for the Utsavar. Dhoopa-Deepa-Naivedyam, Shodasha Upachara Deepadadhanai.
630pm there’s a dance performance followed by an utsava murti veethi ula. The utsavar was taken around the temple, and on a Veethi Purappadu following that. Livestreamed here.

This morning, Arun dropped in to the Siddhi Vinayaka temple on MG Road. The priest tells him he was there for the Manakkula Laksharchanai yesterday. The Vinayaka at this temple is said to be 350 years old, while the plethora of prakara shrines around it have come up later. These include: Murugan, Vishnu, Vaidyanatha Sivalinga, a Nataraja hall, Ayyappan, Hayagriva and some other little ones. The ambience is very cozy. The temple celebrates “all events for all the gods”, says the priest – which is a huge undertaking to say the least. The bull vahana was still out in the corridor from yesterday’s Pradosham ul-purappadu.
The patrikai mentions: Vigneswara puja, Vastu Shanti, Mrtsangrahanam, Ankurarpanam, Yaga Salai 1st kala yaga puja, Purnahuti and Deeparadhanai.

7pm – Just as Arun is about to enter the temple, a host of priests emerge with various thattus and a kalasa. Accompanied by thavil and nadaswaram, they move to the sthalavriksham for an aradhanai. It is a surprise to find the sacred tree in a remote corner, tucked behind the thronging shoe-stand.
The host soon goes back into the temple to prepare for the Shankhabhishekam.

712pm – The stage has the usual panca-Vinayakas at the back, with a homa-kundam in the centre. Right behind the homa-kundam, on a platform, are two conches – one beautiful large white conch with a silver-capped tip, and an even larger conch that is entirely covered by a silver kavacham. The other smaller conches are prepared and kept on the right corner of the stage. A small carpet is laid down for the ubhayakara sankalpam in front of the utsava stage. The rest of the crowd is kept behind by barricades. The man sitting for the sankalpam alongside his wife turns out to be the Maintenance Officer of the temple. Holding an orange in one hand and sacred water in the other, the two are made to repeat chants. The sankalpam concludes with the declaration of the Sahasrashankhabhishekam” that is to begin. Simultaneously, there is a puja offered to a mandala on the floor, quite a distance ahead of the ubhayakaras.

730pm – One priest chants various mantras, in sync with which three other priests, sitting cross-legged, offer pushparchanai. For one instance, the flower is held above the head, then touched to the forehead, heart and both knees, followed by mudras and movements, before tossing flowers into the air. These gestures and hand-movements differ for different mantrams and are all fascinating to watch.
743pm – other on-stage preparations ongoing on and around the shankhas. The ritual practice here seems extensive.
The puja can be watched
on this livestream

We go to the Lakshajapa Homam at 7am, which is Ekadina Laksharchanai on the patrikai. They chant the Vinayaka Sahasranamam. There are 2 priests chanting on stage, but on the speakers we distinctly hear 3 voices – a mystery to which never found an answer! We are vaguely aware of a calculation that determines the number of repetitions of the japa, but don’t yet know the precise details of it. The Sahasrananam is chanted multiple times throughout the day, by multiple priests, which increases the total to be equal to hundred-thousand repetitions.

edits.title: Into the middle of it all

children.text: Deepa goes to the Vasavi Kannika Parameswari temple for the first time, to wander around and find out about its festival calendars. She finds herself in the midst of the Ramar Utsavam! It's quiet in the evening though; whatever pujas have happened, happened in the morning. I decide to return for one tomorrow.
